Troubleshooting
NINJATRADER 8 ERRORS

Problems that come from NinjaTrader itself, such as connection and logon errors, disabled prop accounts, ATM templates, and stuck simulation positions, are on NinjaTrader 8 Troubleshooting.

Alert Latency​

Alert lag or latency can occur before CrossTrade receives a message, during routing, or between broker acceptance and a fill. Compare timestamps for the same alert, in the same time zone:

Signal condition and TradingView alert log: when did the condition occur, and when did TradingView fire? A strategy marker or bar's opening time is not necessarily the alert's firing time. Check bar-close settings, the chart's data delay and the alert's saved script snapshot.
CrossTrade Alert History: when did CrossTrade receive it, and what processing time, destination and result were recorded? A short processing time does not measure how long TradingView took to send it.
Broker order and execution history: when was the order accepted and when did it fill? A resting limit order can be accepted immediately and fill much later.

If you see a ten-minute gap, send support those timestamps, the account, contract, alert condition and time zone. Do not infer a transport delay from a chart marker alone. For Tradovate, check the broker link and any later warning on the accepted alert; NinjaTrader performance settings apply only to the NT8 route.

From TradingView: Alert delays can occasionally occur, especially around the top of the hour and major news announcements where their server load increases. CrossTrade marks the received time exactly, but the time it takes to arrive at our front door is out of our control.

TradingView official response**:** "Unfortunately, currently signals can be sent with a delay (several seconds) at the beginning of trading sessions and at the beginning/end of an hour, because the load on the servers increases. We are already working on this issue and although there is no ETA yet. Please accept our apologies for the inconvenience."

To NinjaTrader: Execution latency can occasionally occur and is influenced by a number of factors like your internet connection and PC specs. There are a number of ways you can optimize NT8 that we outline here and strongly suggest all users consider implementing for the best experience.

Optimizing NinjaTrader Performance

Formatting Issues​

Did you forget the semi colon at the end?
Did you add a semi colon in between accounts when it should be a comma?
Are you missing a required field for your command type?

These are the common reasons you'll see a formatting issue.

Plain text, JSON and unresolved TradingView placeholders​

CrossTrade accepts key=value; commands and flat CrossTrade JSON objects. It does not accept every broker's JSON format or arbitrary nested strategy output. Use the JSON webhook reference for the supported fields. Put only the command in TradingView's Message box: no Markdown fences, introductory sentence or default alert text.

If an error contains literal {{strategy.order.action}}, TradingView did not substitute it. Strategy order-fill placeholders need a strategy order-fill alert; they do not supply buy/sell values for an indicator. {{strategy.order.alert_message}} only forwards the text your Pine order call sets in alert_message. If that text is empty, it does not build a command for you. For an indicator, use its supported alert mechanism and explicit action/quantity, or have the script generate the complete message.

Webhook Trader does not evaluate TradingView variables. Use action=buy; qty=1; there, then test the dynamic version from TradingView. After changing script inputs, recreate the alert. If a closed-source indicator controls its own alert() text and offers no editable Message field, ask its author for CrossTrade-formatted output; pasting a webhook URL alone cannot translate its prose into orders.

A complete static Tradovate entry​

Replace the key and account with your own practice-account values. Execute sends an order, including when used from Webhook Trader.

key=YOUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET;

command=PLACE;

account=YOUR_PRACTICE_ACCOUNT;

instrument=MES1!;

action=BUY;

qty=1;

order_type=MARKET;

tif=DAY;

destination=tradovate;


Keep destination=tradovate; on exits and cancellations too. The account selects the linked broker account; a trial subscription does not force every command into simulation. See first-trade verification.

Always Remember the Semicolon​

key=my-secret-key;
command=place;
account=sim101;
instrument=ES 12-26;
action=buy;
qty=1;
order_type=market;
tif=day;

Separate Multiple Accounts by Comma​

****key=my-secret-key;
command=place;
account=sim101,sim102,sim103;
instrument=ES 12-26;
action=buy;qty=1;
order_type=market;
tif=day;

Use the Full Account Name​

Examples:
(NT Sim) account=sim101;
(NT Demo) account=demo123456789;

Use All the Required Fields​

NinjaTrader's available commands require (R) certain fields be present for the command to be implemented.

For example a PLACE command requires the Account, Instrument, Action, Qty, Order Type and TIF (time in force) to be present.

key=my-secret-key; ``- Required by CrossTrade
command=place; ``- Required by NinjaTrader
account=sim101; ``- Required by NinjaTrader
instrument=ES 12-26; ``- Required by NinjaTrader
action=buy; ``- Required By NinjaTrader
qty=1; ``- Required by NinjaTrader
order_type=market; ``- Required by NinjaTrader
tif=day; ``- Required by NinjaTrader

Every command's required and optional fields are in the Available Commands table.

No Market Data to Drive the Simulation​

If you submit an alert with an expired contract, you'll encounter this error message. \ Error - [Account], There is no market data available to drive the simulation engine. affected Order:
Be sure to update your alerts to the front month contract after rollover to ensure you're submitting orders on an active contract.

Clearing a Sim Position on an Expired Contract​

If a position on the expired contract is stuck in a simulation account, reset the account in NinjaTrader. The steps are on NinjaTrader 8 Troubleshooting.

Symbology not matching for Canceling Orders​

In your NinjaTrader settings, you can set the Symbology display style. This setting MUST match the format you are using when attempting to cancel pending orders.

If your setting is Numeric, then you need to submit the request in the numeric format: ES 12-25

Something Went Wrong, check message format​

This error message is usually an indication that you have supplied a partial contract amount; which NinjaTrader does not support. In the example below you can see 3.664901 is the qty for this command, which NT8 rejects.

A round number of contracts or shares is required.

Test Resources​

These two TradingView resources are designed to help troubleshoot by firing alerts quickly.

TradingView Test Indicator​

To help with Troubleshooting issues we offer a free TradingView indicator that will force signals to be generated on every bar. When using this with the trigger "Once per bar close" each bar will send a single alert.

Be sure to also use the "flatten_first=true;" in your Alert Message so that each bar opens a new position.

https://www.tradingview.com/script/pXjxZz6z-XT-Troubleshooting-Indicator/

TradingView Test Strategy​

Similarly to the Test Indicator, this strategy is designed to provide a code example of how to establish buy and sell signals that utilize the {{strategy.order.action}} variable, as well as provide a way to test your alerts using the variable in place of the BUY or SELL in your Action field. (e.g. action={{strategy.order.action}} vs. action=BUY;)

INFO

Each pine script strategy is coded differently and the strategy.order.action variable is not a default in all strategies.

https://www.tradingview.com/script/P2tUeSKr-XT-Strategy-Help/
